title: ExeBench-FHD: Addressing Fidelity Issues in Decompiler Evaluation
title_zh: ExeBench-FHD：解决反编译器评测中的保真度问题

paragraphs.en: ExeBench is one of the most widely used benchmarks for evaluating LLM-based decompilers. We analyze ExeBench and identify nine issues that affect how faithfully a test measures a decompiler. Three of them prevent LLM decompilers from recovering C code from ExeBench’s function. These are ambiguous parameter order when integer and floating-point types are mixed, unused parameters that optimized assembly may drop, and constants stored outside the function’s assembly code. Six more affect test validity: non-void functions without a return, placeholder types, static or inline functions removed by the optimizer, functions named main , trivial bodies and truncated definitions. We present ExeBench-FHD , a backward-compatible revision of ExeBench that adds 16 new fields: call-site assembly, data sections, test wrappers, linked-binary disassembly and five warning flags. In ExeBench, 38.9% of functions have at least one of the five flags; dropping records with any of the four warning flags (all except unused_param , which marks functions that the new wrappers make evaluable) keeps 63.9% of the corpus. In an evaluation at -O2 on four architectures, the new fields raise GPT 6 Sol’s re-execution rate by up to 26.5%, 19.1% and 21.0% on functions that read data sections, mix parameter types and have unused parameters, respectively.
paragraphs.zh: ExeBench 是评估基于 LLM 的反编译器最广泛使用的基准测试之一。 我们分析了 ExeBench，并识别出九个影响测试对反编译器测量忠实度的问题。 其中三个问题阻止 LLM 反编译器从 ExeBench 的函数恢复 C 代码。 这些问题是：整数类型和浮点类型混合时参数顺序的歧义、优化后的汇编可能丢弃的未使用参数，以及存储在函数汇编代码之外的常量。 另外六个问题影响测试的有效性：没有返回值的非 void 函数、占位符类型、被优化器移除的 static 或 inline 函数、名为 main 的函数、平凡函数体以及被截断的定义。 我们提出了 ExeBench-FHD，这是 ExeBench 的一个向后兼容的修订版，新增了 16 个字段：调用点汇编、数据段、测试包装器、链接后二进制文件的反汇编以及五个警告标志。 在 ExeBench 中，38.9% 的函数至少带有五个标志中的一个；剔除带有四个警告标志（除 unused_param 外，该标志标记的函数在新包装器下变得可评估）中任意一个的记录后，仍保留语料库的 63.9%。 在四 种架构上以 -O2 进行的评估中，新字段使 GPT 6 Sol 在读取数据段、混合参数类型和带有未使用参数的函数上的重执行率分别提升高达 26.5%、19.1% 和 21.0%。

paragraphs.en: Binary decompilation is the process of recovering source code from a compiled binary, and it is a core step in reverse engineering. Compilation is a lossy process. Information that helps humans understand code, such as variable names, data types, comments and macro definitions, is transformed or removed; the higher the level of binary optimization, the harder the binary is to understand. Commercial and open-source decompilers such as IDA Pro ( Hex-Rays SA, 2024 ) and Ghidra ( National Security Agency, 2019 ) use algorithms and heuristics to recover source code from the binary, but their output still deviates from the original source code.

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently grown popular not only for coding but also for decompilation. Researchers have proposed approaches that use LLMs in decompilation pipelines ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ; Armengol-Estapé et al., 2024 ; Tan et al., 2024 ) . However, only a few datasets contain both source code and the corresponding assembly. These include AnghaBench ( da Silva et al., 2021 ) , ExeBench ( Armengol-Estapé et al., 2022 ) , HumanEval-Decompile ( Tan et al., 2024 ) , and, most recently, DecompileBench ( Gao et al., 2025 ) and Decompile-Bench ( Tan et al., 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）近来不仅因编程而流行，也因反编译而受到关注。 研究者已提出在反编译流水线中使用大语言模型的方法（Wang et al., 2026；Jiang et al., 2025；Armengol-Estapé et al., 2024；Tan et al., 2024）。 然而，只有少数数据集同时包含源代码和对应的汇编代码。 这些数据集包括 AnghaBench（da Silva et al., 2021）、ExeBench（Armengol-Estapé et al., 2022）、HumanEval-Decompile（Tan et al., 2024），以及最近的 DecompileBench（Gao et al., 2025）和 Decompile-Bench（Tan et al., 2025）。

paragraphs.en: Among these, ExeBench is one of the most widely used for training and testing. It contains 6.56M C functions from GitHub and AnghaBench, split into ten training, validation and test sets ( Table 1 ), and most are stand-alone compilable. Each function comes with assembly for x86 and ARM and with input-output (IO) examples. ExeBench also provides a script for evaluating decompilers on its test splits: the decompiled function is recompiled, linked into a test wrapper that feeds it each example input, and checked against the corresponding expected output.
paragraphs.zh: 其中，ExeBench 是目前训练和测试中使用最广泛的数据集之一。 它包含来自 GitHub 和 AnghaBench 的 656 万个 C 函数，划分为十个训练集、验证集和测试集（表 1），且大多数函数可独立编译。 每个函数都附带 x86 和 ARM 架构的汇编代码以及输入输出（IO）示例。 ExeBench 还提供了一个在其测试集上评估反编译器的脚本：反编译出的函数会被重新编译，链接到一个向其逐个输入示例输入的测试包装程序中，并与相应的预期输出进行比对检查。

paragraphs.en: To utilize this test to fairly measure a decompiler, the input should contain what the function needs to be re-created, namely the function’s signature (parameter order and count) and any constants it reads. The wrapper calls the function with its original signature, but ExeBench’s assembly of the compiled function may not retain the parameter order, unused parameters and constant values. This is a problem with the evaluation, not with the decompiler.

Functions often require information that a binary in practice has, but the assembly in the dataset does not: real-world binaries also contain callers and data sections, whereas ExeBench provides only the function’s own body. Consequently, a test failure on ExeBench does not (necessarily) indicate a decompiler made a mistake. We call these fidelity issues affecting evaluations.

paragraphs.en: We identify nine fidelity issues ( Table 2 ). In three of them, the function’s assembly in ExeBench lacks information that in practice a binary provides: mixed integer and floating-point parameters (P1, 1.5% of the corpus but 11.5% of test_real ), unused parameters that the optimizer may remove (P2, 7.6% of the corpus) and constants stored in data sections (P3, 16.2% at -O2 ). Two make the test oracle unreliable: non-void functions without a return (P4, 1.7%) and placeholder types (P5, 9.3%). Three prevent a usable source–assembly pair: static or inline functions, which the optimizer may remove at higher optimization levels (P6, 36.3%); functions named main , which fail to link with the driver main (P7, 6.3%); and truncated definitions, which fail to compile (P9, 0.6%). Finally, trivial bodies (P8, 27.8%) are easy to decompile and raise average scores.

paragraphs.en: To address these issues, we introduce ExeBench-FHD 1 1 1 FHD abbreviates Fidélité de Haute Décompilation, French for ”high decompilation fidelity”. , a backward-compatible revision of ExeBench that adds 16 new fields and modifies none of the existing ones. The new fields supply the parts of the binary that the function’s assembly leaves out alongside the assembly ( Section 3 ): data sections for constants (P3), call-site assembly (the assembly code of a function call) for parameter order (P1), and test wrappers that accept either all parameters or only the used ones (P2). They also provide disassembly regenerated from the linked binary and five warning flags for the remaining issues. Each field that depends on compilation has a diagnostic field recording why it is empty. Because no inherited field changes, existing ExeBench pipelines keep working and can adopt the new fields one at a time ( Section 4 ).

sents.en: They also provide disassembly regenerated from the linked binary and five warning flags for the remaining issues.
sents.zh: 它们还提供了从链接后的二进制文件重新生成的反汇编代码，以及针对其余问题的五个警告标志。

sents.en: Because no inherited field changes, existing ExeBench pipelines keep working and can adopt the new fields one at a time ( Section 4 ).

paragraphs.en: For the decompilation task, there are only a handful of datasets for both training and testing. AnghaBench ( da Silva et al., 2021 ) is a collection of 1 million C functions scraped from GitHub. It uses the type-inference tool Psyche-C ( Melo et al., 2017 ) to add missing external dependencies, so that each function can be compiled into an object file. However, since Psyche-C only declares the dependencies, GCC treats them as forward declarations: it produces an object file but cannot link it into an executable.
paragraphs.zh: 对于反编译任务而言，可用于训练和测试的数据集只有寥寥数个。 AnghaBench（da Silva 等，2021）是从 GitHub 上抓取的 100 万个 C 函数的集合。 它使用类型推断工具 Psyche-C（Melo 等，2017）来补充缺失的外部依赖，从而将每个函数编译为目标文件。 然而，由于 Psyche-C 只是声明了这些依赖，GCC 会将它们视为前置声明：它能生成目标文件，却无法将其链接成可执行文件。

paragraphs.en: Armengol-Estapé et al. (2022) observe the need for an executable dataset for machine learning and introduce ExeBench , whose source functions are scraped from GitHub and which extends AnghaBench by adding dependencies to the C code. ExeBench walks through each function’s repository to find the relevant dependencies and turns the function into a stand-alone compilable file. If the dependencies are not present in the repository, ExeBench searches a larger GitHub dataset, and if more than one repository has the same definition, it chooses the one with more stars. If the real dependencies are not available on GitHub, synthetic definitions are generated and injected into the code. ExeBench also provides IO examples, produced by an automatic generator that synthesizes inputs for each parameter type from the function signature using a seed and records the outputs.

paragraphs.en: In 2025, two benchmarks with similar names appeared. Decompile-Bench ( Tan et al., 2025 ) contains two million binary-source function pairs mined from binaries compiled from permissively licensed GitHub projects. It uses a source-trace algorithm based on DWARF ( DWARF Debugging Information Format Committee, 2017 ) and tree-sitter ( Brunsfeld and Tree-Sitter Contributors, 2024 ) to match each assembly function to its source function. The dataset has an uneven number of assembly versions per source function (1 to 6), and the released data lacks the optimization-level field and generation code, so we cannot determine the cause.
paragraphs.zh: 2025 年，出现了两个名称相似的基准测试。 Decompile-Bench（Tan 等，2025）包含从采用宽松许可证的 GitHub 项目编译得到的二进制文件中挖掘出的两百万个二进制—源码函数对。 它使用基于 DWARF（DWARF 调试信息格式委员会，2017）和 tree-sitter（Brunsfeld 与 Tree-Sitter 贡献者，2024）的源码追踪算法，将每个汇编函数匹配到其对应的源码函数。 该数据集中每个源码函数对应的汇编版本数量不均衡（1 到 6 个），且发布的数据缺少优化级别字段和生成代码，因此我们无法确定其原因。

paragraphs.en: DecompileBench ( Gao et al., 2025 ) selects around 20k functions from 130 OSS-Fuzz ( Serebryany, 2017 ) projects, keeping those that a fuzzer can trigger. Like ExeBench, it extracts each function’s dependencies and builds a shared library containing it. A decompiled function is rebuilt into a library and counts as correct if re-running the fuzzer with the same seed gives the same output as the original. However, its assembly is generated from object code rather than a linked binary, so call targets and data references remain unresolved relocations. ExeBench-FHD avoids this by disassembling linked executables.
paragraphs.zh: DecompileBench（Gao 等，2025）从 130 个 OSS-Fuzz（Serebryany，2017）项目中选取约 2 万个函数，保留模糊测试器能够触发的那些函数。 与 ExeBench 类似，它提取每个函数的依赖项，并构建包含该函数的共享库。 反编译得到的函数会被重新构建为库，如果用相同种子重新运行模糊测试器得到的输出与原始输出一致，则计为正确。 然而，其汇编代码是由目标代码生成的，而非来自链接后的二进制文件，因此调用目标和数据引用仍然是未解析的重定位项。 ExeBench-FHD 通过对链接后的可执行文件进行反汇编来避免这一问题。

paragraphs.en: On 32-bit Intel (x86), function arguments are passed on the stack, which preserves their order regardless of type. On 64-bit Intel, 32-bit ARM and 64-bit ARM, however, parameters are passed in different sets of registers depending on their data type. Table 3 shows how each architecture passes parameters ( Lu et al., 2025 ; Arm Limited, 2026b ; Arm Limited, 2026a ) . In ExeBench’s test_real split, 11.5% of functions have mixed parameter types (1.5% of the corpus). If their parameter order is not recovered correctly, the corresponding test fail.

paragraphs.en: If all parameters have the same data type (first two functions of ), LLM-based decompilers can potentially identify the parameter order from the register sequence. However, if a function mixes data types, such as int and float (last two functions of ), the order cannot be recovered from the function’s assembly alone (as in ExeBench). This limitation occurs because each data type uses a separate register sequence. For example, the System V x86-64 Application Binary Interface (ABI) ( Lu et al., 2025 ) independently allocates integer arguments are assigned to [ rdi , rsi , …] and floating-point arguments to [ xmm0 , xmm1 , …].

paragraphs.en: A function taking an int followed by a float , and one taking a float followed by an int , therefore read the same registers and compile to identical assembly. paragraphs.en: Some ExeBench functions do not use all of their parameters. In , sum is declared with three parameters, a , b and c , but the C source only uses a and c . At O0 , all three parameters are visible in the function’s assembly. At higher optimization levels the callee never reads the unused argument, and the compiler handles it in one of two ways. In some builds it keeps each used parameter in its original register, so the assembly still implies all three parameters ( a in rdi , c in rdx ). In others it moves the used parameters into the first registers, so the assembly implies only two ( a in rdi , c in rsi ). Which happens depends on the build, even for the same source function, so a decompiler faithful to the assembly can legitimately recover either form, and a test that evaluates one marks the other as wrong. In a real-world binary, the callers of an externally visible function still pass all three arguments, but ExeBench does not provide them.

paragraphs.en: ExeBench is built around stand-alone, executable source-assembly pairs. To achieve this, it mines dependencies from each function’s GitHub repository and, when none are found, injects dummy dependencies generated with Psyche-C. Around 9.3% of the corpus contains functions with dummy user-defined type (UDT) definitions ( ). Since these placeholder types carry no real content, the source-assembly pair is not faithful to the original program. A test on such a function checks the placeholder rather than the real type.

paragraphs.en: Based on our analysis of ExeBench, we group the identified issues into two categories. (1) Issues where the assembly in ExeBench lacks information that a real-world binary provides, which can affect downstream uses such as LLM-based decompilation (P1–P3). (2) Issues that affect what a test outcome means or whether a function can be evaluated at all (P4–P9). ExeBench-FHD addresses each with a new field or flag, described below. ExeBench-FHD preserves ExeBench’s licensing and our added fields are released under the MIT license.
paragraphs.zh: 基于我们对 ExeBench 的分析，我们将发现的问题归为两类。 （1）ExeBench 中的汇编缺少真实世界二进制文件所提供的信息的问题，这类问题会影响基于 LLM 的反编译等下游用途（P1–P3）。 （2）影响测试结果含义或决定函数是否可以被评估的问题（P4–P9）。 ExeBench-FHD 通过新增的字段或标志分别应对这些问题，具体描述如下。 ExeBench-FHD 保留 ExeBench 的许可证，我们新增的字段以 MIT 许可证发布。

paragraphs.en: ExeBench-FHD follows two design principles. The first is additivity : existing ExeBench fields are not modified; every fix or flag is added as a new field, so ExeBench-FHD is a drop-in replacement for ExeBench and existing pipelines keep working. The second is flagging over filtering : for some problems, we add flags instead of modifying or filtering the dataset, leaving downstream users free to decide how to handle each issue.

paragraphs.en: The main issue is P1: parameter order is ambiguous when a function has at least one floating-point parameter ( float , double ) and at least one integer or pointer parameter. To solve this, we introduce a new field, func_call , which holds the assembly of a call to the function on all four architectures: x86, x86-64, ARM32 and ARM64. On x86, arguments are pushed onto the stack from right to left, so the first parameter ends up at the lowest address; the push order and the callee’s stack offsets are therefore enough to recover the parameter order. On the other three architectures, the driver derives each argument from argv in declaration order, so the call site shows which argument is loaded into which register and thus the order of the parameters.
paragraphs.zh: 主要问题是 P1：当函数同时含有至少一个浮点参数（float、double）和至少一个整数或指针参数时，参数顺序会有歧义。 为了解决这个问题，我们引入一个新字段 func_call，它保存对该函数在四种架构（x86、x86-64、ARM32 和 ARM64）上调用所生成的汇编代码。 在 x86 上，参数按从右到左的顺序压入栈中，因此第一个参数最终位于最低地址；压栈顺序与被调用者的栈偏移量足以恢复参数顺序。 在其他三种架构上，驱动程序按声明顺序从 argv 推导每个参数，因此调用点能够表明哪个参数被加载到哪个寄存器中，从而确定参数的顺序。

paragraphs.en: About 7.6% of ExeBench functions have unused parameters (P2). In ExeBench, each function has a C++ test wrapper ( real_exe_wrapper , angha_exe_wrapper ) that reads the function’s IO examples according to its parameter count (from the signature field). When functions are compiled at O1 or above, however, the assembly may imply all parameters or only the used ones, depending on the build. A decompiler that recovers only the used parameters fails against this harness, which passes every parameter, used or unused. We therefore introduce two new C++ wrappers, opt_real_exe_wrapper and opt_angha_exe_wrapper , that accept either form.
paragraphs.zh: ExeBench 中约 7.6% 的函数存在未使用的参数（P2）。 在 ExeBench 中，每个函数都有一个 C++ 测试包装器（real_exe_wrapper、angha_exe_wrapper），它会根据参数数量（来自签名字段）读取该函数的 IO 示例。 然而，当函数以 O1 或更高级别编译时，汇编代码可能隐含全部参数，也可能只隐含被使用的参数，这取决于构建方式。 只恢复被使用参数的反编译器无法通过这种测试框架，因为该框架会传入每一个参数，无论其是否被使用。 因此，我们引入了两个新的 C++ 包装器，opt_real_exe_wrapper 和 opt_angha_exe_wrapper，它们可以接受上述任一形式。

paragraphs.en: As described in P3, data is stored in several sections, and the .text section only contains references to it. We therefore introduce a data_section field for all four architectures (x86, x86-64, ARM32 and ARM64), which holds the contents of every relevant section that is present ( .data , .rodata , .bss , etc.). Since not every record compiles, data_section is present only for records that build.

paragraphs.en: Issues P4–P9 do not hide information from the decompiler, but they affect what a test outcome means or whether a function can be evaluated. For P4, P5, P8 and P9, we add separate flag fields rather than modifying the dataset. These flags let users exclude such functions or report them separately during evaluation. For P6 and P7, a new script (released with the dataset) produces the objdump_asm field. It regenerates each function’s assembly from the linked binary (the .out file), whereas ExeBench’s asm field is generated from the .o file. The script supports all four architectures (x86, x86-64, ARM32 and ARM64).

paragraphs.en: We use GPT 6 Sol, a frontier commercial model, as such with no training on ExeBench’s format for decompilation. If a model of this strength still fails on P1–P3, the cause is the information in the input, not model capacity. We call the model twice for decompilation: once with just the function’s assembly ( asm ) code, and once with the assembly code along with the data_section and func_call ( +ctx , where ctx is short for the added context, i.e. data_section and func_call ). The only difference between the two runs is the added context in the input. The results therefore show what the added fields make possible; they do not rank decompilers or show how iterative or agentic pipelines would behave.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 GPT 6 Sol 这一前沿商业模型，按其原始形式使用，未针对 ExeBench 的反编译格式进行任何训练。 如果如此强大的模型仍然在 P1–P3 上失败，原因就在于输入中的信息，而非模型能力。 我们对模型进行两次调用来完成反编译：一次仅提供函数的汇编（asm）代码，一次提供汇编代码以及 data_section 和 func_call（+ctx，其中 ctx 是新增上下文的简称，即 data_section 和 func_call）。 两次运行之间唯一的区别是输入中新增的上下文。 因此，这些结果显示的是新增字段所能带来的作用；它们并非对反编译器的排名，也不能反映迭代式或智能体式流水线的表现。

paragraphs.en: We use test_real , ExeBench’s test split with real dependencies (2,134 functions), compiled with GCC at -O2 , a level commonly used for released software. GPT 6 Sol (default settings, one answer per function) decompiles each function twice: under ( asm ), and ( +ctx ). We keep every function that can be built and tested on a given architecture, 1,657–1,857 per architecture; functions with an unused parameter, identified by the unused_param flag, are scored separately. A decompiled function re-executes if, compiled into ExeBench’s test wrapper, it reproduces the expected output on every IO example; the re-execution rate is the share of functions that do. To check that a gain is not due to chance, we use an exact paired sign test (also known as the exact McNemar test), which compares only the functions whose outcome changes between the two runs (details in Appendix E ).

paragraphs.en: For mixed-type parameters, the call-site assembly in func_call shows which argument is loaded into which register, and thus the parameter order. Without it, the asm-only predictions often have the wrong parameter order or count and do not compile against the test wrapper. With context, re-compilation rises by 13–20% on the three register architectures, and re-execution rises by 12–19%. x86, which passes arguments on the stack in order, gains least (+9.8%) ( Table 21 ).
paragraphs.zh: 对于混合类型的参数，func_call 中的调用点汇编代码展示了哪个实参被加载到哪个寄存器，从而可以确定参数顺序。 没有它时，仅基于汇编的预测常常出现参数顺序或数量错误，无法针对测试包装器完成编译。 加入上下文后，三种寄存器架构上的重新编译率提升了 13–20%，重新执行率提升了 12–19%。x86 由于按顺序通过栈传递参数，提升最少（+9.8%）（表 21）。

paragraphs.en: ExeBench-FHD ’s wrapper ( opt_real_exe_wrapper ) is executed to test if a decompiled code executes correctly. Our modified wrapper contains two separate function call wrappers. One with all the parameters used in the original source code and one with only the parameters used in the function after compiler optimizations. This enables us to cater for various disassembler behaviours based on what it infers from the assembly pattern implications. Our wrapper raises the re-execution on functions with unused parameters by 17–21%, from 58–64% to 76–82% ( Table 18 ; p < 10 − 3 p<10^{-3} on every architecture). The call-site assembly helps here because it shows how many arguments the caller passes, which the function’s own assembly does not.

paragraphs.en: We analyzed all 6.56M functions in ExeBench and found nine fidelity issues: three cases of missing context, where normal compilation removes information that ExeBench’s tests still expect, and six warning-level issues. ExeBench-FHD added the missing context as new fields and added warning flags for the rest. The added context raised GPT 6 Sol’s re-execution rate by up to 26.5% on the affected functions. Because we focus on evaluation and give a single general-purpose LLM the context in a single pass, the gains isolate the effect of the context itself. This sets up two natural next steps: testing whether agents can retrieve this context on their own, and whether training decompilers with func_call or data_section improves them. We hope this work encourages the community to treat evaluation fidelity as a priority in decompilation benchmarks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们分析了 ExeBench 中全部 656 万个函数，发现了九个保真度问题：其中三个属于缺失上下文，即常规编译会移除 ExeBench 测试仍依赖的信息；其余六个属于警告级别问题。 ExeBench-FHD 将缺失的上下文补充为新字段，并为其余问题添加了警告标志。 新增的上下文使 GPT 6 Sol 在受影响函数上的重新执行率最高提升了 26.5%。 由于我们专注于评估，并让单个通用 LLM 在单次过程中获得上下文，因此这些提升可以单独归因于上下文本身的作用。 这为两个自然的后续方向奠定了基础：一是测试智能体能否自行检索这些上下文，二是考察使用 func_call 或 data_section 训练反编译器能否改进其性能。 我们希望这项工作能促使社区将评估保真度视为反编译基准测试中的优先事项。

paragraphs.en: ExeBench-FHD has three main limitations. First, every compilation-dependent field ( func_call , data_section and objdump_asm ) is built with GCC only, so the assembly and data sections may differ from what other compilers such as Clang emit. Second, ExeBench-FHD inherits limitations of ExeBench that we leave for future work. About 55% of records fail to link because ExeBench does not capture their dependencies, so these fields are sparse on the synth splits ( Table 22 ). The func_call generator skips unsupported parameter types and functions named main (16.4% of the corpus: 10.1% and 6.3% respectively, Table 24 ) and uses a generated driver instead of the function’s real callers. We also flag issues without repairing the source, such as signature fields that disagree with the function definition ( Table 10 ). Third, the warning flags are rules of thumb: trivial_function depends on a line-count cutoff that is a design choice ( Figure 2 ), and no_return and truncated_funcs use syntactic checks that can miss or misfire on some cases.
paragraphs.zh: ExeBench-FHD 存在三个主要局限。 首先，所有依赖编译的字段（func_call、data_section 和 objdump_asm）均仅使用 GCC 构建，因此其汇编和数据段可能与 Clang 等其他编译器生成的结果不同。 其次，ExeBench-FHD 继承了 ExeBench 的局限，我们将其留待未来工作解决。 约 55% 的记录因 ExeBench 未捕获其依赖关系而无法链接，因此这些字段在合成数据划分上是稀疏的（表 22）。 func_call 生成器会跳过不受支持的参数类型以及名为 main 的函数（占语料库的 16.4%：分别为 10.1% 和 6.3%，见表 24），并使用生成的驱动程序来代替该函数的真实调用者。 我们还会标记问题而不修复源代码，例如签名与函数定义不一致的字段（表 10）。 第三，警告标志只是经验法则：trivial_function 依赖于一个作为设计选择的代码行数阈值（图 2），而 no_return 和 truncated_funcs 使用的语法检查在某些情况下可能会漏检或误报。

paragraphs.en: The disassembled subset is more trivial than the corpus (39.7% vs. 27.8% flagged trivial_function ), because short, self-contained functions are the ones most likely to build. paragraphs.en: trivial_function flags a body that is empty, a single return statement, or at most two non-blank, non-comment lines. Over the corpus, every record whose body has at most two lines is flagged (1,803,896 records). The remaining 23,797 flagged records (0.36%) are single return statements that span more than two lines. Figure 2 shows how the share of non-trivial records (those a user keeps after dropping trivial ones) changes as the line cutoff is raised. The share falls steadily, with no point where it suddenly drops, so the cutoff is a trade-off rather than a property of the data. train_real_simple_io is the most trivial split at every cutoff, and train_not_compilable the least. Requiring the body to also be branch-free (no if / for / while / switch ) flattens the curves: at a 10-line cutoff, 53.4% of test_real is still non-trivial, against 24.8% under the line-count rule without it.

paragraphs.en: We decompile the -O2 build of every test_real function that can be prompted and evaluated on a given architecture (it has IO examples, a test wrapper, a successful objdump_asm and a func_call ), using GPT 6 Sol with its default decoding settings and one sample per function. The system prompt, the assembly and the output format are identical in both conditions; only the context block differs. A prediction re-compiles if it builds inside the function’s test wrapper, and re-executes if the resulting program reproduces the expected output on every IO example. paragraphs.en: For the functions that read at least one byte outside .text ( Table 20 ), the context raises re-execution by 19.5% on x86-64, 18.1 on x86 and 26.5 on ARM64 ( p < 10 − 5 p<10^{-5} each). paragraphs.en: For functions whose signature mixes floating-point and integer (including char ) or pointer parameters ( Table 21 ), the context raises re-execution by 19.1% on ARM64, 17.0 on x86-64 and 12.5 on ARM32 ( p < 10 − 3 p<10^{-3} each). Its standard calling convention (cdecl, short for C declaration) passes all arguments on the stack in declaration order, so the assembly already yields the signature: asm-only re-compilation is 88.7% on x86, against 60–63% on the other three architectures. paragraphs.en: The same constant does not always end up as the same bytes in the data section on every architecture. Among records where all four architectures produced a .rodata section, that section is byte-identical on all four in 45.4% of cases over all splits (208,405 of 459,033 sections). This rises to 63.6% on valid_real (28 of 44) and is 42.1% on train_real_compilable . This is expected rather than a defect. ARM can build many constants directly from instruction immediates instead of storing them in memory, and pointer width and alignment differ between the 32-bit and 64-bit targets. This is why data_section is stored per architecture rather than once per record.

paragraphs.en: Table 24 breaks the func_call outcome down by how many of the four architectures succeeded. Over all splits, 7.5% of records build on all four and 16.4% are never attempted: 10.1% have a parameter type the call-site generator does not support (struct or union by value, SIMD vector, _Complex , etc.) and 6.3% are functions named main . Records that succeed on exactly two architectures (12.5% of the corpus) are almost all concentrated in the synthetic-dependency splits. On test_synth and valid_synth , every one of the 3,586 two-architecture records succeeds on x86-64 and ARM64 and fails on both 32-bit targets, for a single reason: the synthetic dependency header generated for these splits declares typedef unsigned long size_t , which conflicts with the 32-bit C library’s unsigned int definition. Only 0.15% of the corpus builds on the x86 targets but not the ARM targets, and 0.01% on the ARM targets but not the x86 targets. Their errors cluster around inline assembly and special built-in functions for hardware input/output ports that exist on one instruction set only.

paragraphs.en: Across the 43,348,789 non-empty (record, architecture, optimization level) disassembly instances, the median is 16 instruction lines, the mean 33.7, and the 99th percentile 247. 50,475 records (0.77%) have at least one instance over 300 lines. The largest remaining instance has 254,806 lines ( Integrand_3loop_fun33 , a generated function for numerical integration, at x86-64 -O0 ).

paragraphs.en: One record, GCC’s gcc.dg/long-branch-middle.c , is excluded from Table 25 . Its body is a single inline-assembly directive, .fill 32*1024*1024, 4, 0x12345678 , which emits 33,554,432 four-byte words (about 134 MB) of filler. objdump cannot tell this filler from code and disassembles it into 33.5 million instruction lines, about 10 6 10^{6} times the corpus mean of 33.7. We therefore omit objdump_asm for this record. A search for similar constructs among the 50,475 oversized records ( .fill / .space / .skip / .zero / .rept directives, long runs of data directives, or a path inside a compiler test suite) matches only 668 (1.3%). Of these, 620 are compiler test-suite files and 48 contain data-emitting assembly. The very large functions are therefore mostly genuine code, not artificial compiler stress tests.
